entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It has been argued by learned counsel for the appellant that the appellant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in crime in question.
He would submit that the prosecution has failed to prove the case against the appellant and there are omissions and contradictions in the statement of prosecution witnesses.
The appellant is in jail since 30.4.2019.
Hence, he may be released on bail.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the State opposes the prayer for grant of bail and submits that the appellant after enticing minor victim/prosecurtrix, aged about 09 years, to give money, took her to his house and committed forcible sexual intercourse with her.

He would further submit victim prosecutrix has clearly stated about the act committed by the appellant to her which is supported by the MLC Report (Ex-P/12), wherein the doctor has reported that intercourse has been done with the child.
In FSL Report (Ex-P/20) also it has been reported that human spermatozoa were present in the vaginal slides and undergarment of the victim/prosecutrix.
Hence, looking to the manner in which the appellant has committed the act with a victim child, he is not liable to be released on bail.
We have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the records of the Court below.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence available on record, particularly considering the statement of the minor victim/prosecutrix, aged about 09 years, which is supported by medical report (MLC report Ex-P/12), wherein the doctor has reported that intercourse has been done with the child, and further considering the FSL Report (Ex-P/20), in which it is reported that human spermatozoa were present in the vaginal slides and undergarment of the victim/prosecutrix,

further considering the manner in which the appellant has committed the offence with the victim/prosecutrix, her age, we are of the considered opinion that it is not a fit case to suspend the jail sentences.
Accordingly, IA No. 2 of 2023, application filed on behalf of appellant Jassu @ Jasvindar stands rejected.
Let the matter be listed for final hearing.

Sd/- Sd/-
 (Naresh Kumar Chandravanshi) (Ramesh Sinha)
